Definition: from G4862 and G2767; to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate:--mix with, temper together.
BiblicalUsage: The word preached did not profit those in the wilderness, not being mixed with faith in those who heard it, and Paul says God has tempered the body together, giving more abundant honour to the part that lacked. Mixing with faith is what makes the word profit, and tempering together is what makes the body one.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word profits only when mixed with faith, and I believe God tempers His body together so that no part is despised.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
